### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object), runtimeTypes (symbol, a field of const object AUTHORING_RULES))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via validateFormLayout (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `195fce740d54c188a67c7d75e61112a0d7c99267` — the merge of head `6266ec855994fe6b126f7d8f75a602bb1eb7417a` into base `7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 195fce740d54c188a67c7d75e61112a0d7c99267 && git checkout 195fce740d54c188a67c7d75e61112a0d7c99267
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee 6266ec855994fe6b126f7d8f75a602bb1eb7417a && git checkout -B drift-repro 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee && git merge --no-ff 6266ec855994fe6b126f7d8f75a602bb1eb7417a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `6266ec855994fe6b126f7d8f75a602bb1eb7417a`
Local-runs: none

Face: the PR's nine paths decide no face (`record-recognisers.mjs --paths` on the file list); the changeset's line reads `Clause-②: no` with no `(narrowing)` arm, so the declaration face is served at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Read: the net diff against `main` at `7f277a86`, card #29309 with every comment (claim 6578091400, amendment 6579089637, reports 6579051645 and 6579936678), the precedent's pins in `protocol.form-layout-diagnostics.test.ts` (#29196 / PR #29307), and the cited code in the head tree: `packages/lint/src/validate-form-layout.ts`, `view-walk.ts`, `object-field-groups.ts`, `runtime-gate.ts` (`buildRuntimeWriteSnapshotSet`, `runRules`, `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts` (`judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules`, `draftPublishVerdict`), `protocol-stored-collection-fold.ts`, `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` (`evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate`), `metadata-diagnostics.ts` (`itemRelativeIssuePath`, `withPublishVerdict`, `withFormLayoutWarnings`), the four gate call sites in `protocol.ts` (active save 16834, per-item publish 18733, batch publish 19649/19842, restore via `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses`), the view read at `protocol.ts` 5466-5490, and `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`listItems` 7497, `getAllObjects` 6134, `resolveObject` 4541). Check-runs on the head: every run completed, 0 failed, 0 in progress (success on Build Core, Test Core 1-8, Lint and Repo Gates, both Type Check lanes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Dogfood Regression Gate; the skipped ones are opt-in or schedule lanes).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Registration moves to `CLI_AND_RUNTIME` + `runtimeTypes: ['view']`, entry only** — right. The diff touches that one entry in `AUTHORING_RULES`; `tier: 'advisory'`, `commands: ALL`, `input: 'parsed'` and `run` are unchanged. `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('view')` now includes it; registry order puts it after `validateReferenceIntegrity` and before `validatePublicFormFileFields`, which is where the five rule-list pins put it.
2. **The snapshot carries the bound object on every door that runs the rule** — right, by the tree, not only by the dev's boot table. All four doors (active save, per-item publish, batch publish, restore) reach `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules`, which builds `objects` once: `registry.listItems('object')`, which is `getAllObjects()` → `resolveObject()` (the overlay-or-owner base with every `extend` contributor folded, the shape `getObject` serves), then `foldStoredCollection` folds the active `sys_metadata` object rows with the registry's extenders folded onto them. A stored `object_extension` row is registered as an `extend` contributor on every sync (`registerObjectExtension`, `protocol.ts` 1949), so a tenant-authored extension field is in both the gate's universe and the read's. The batch door adds its own pending drafts (`pending`, folded in `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate`), so a view published beside its object in one batch sees that object. Where the object can be absent — outside the write's package closure (`narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`), still a draft outside this batch, or a registry/store read that failed (best-effort, warned) — both checks skip: `objectFields.get(objName)` is `undefined` so (a) never fires, and `checkSectionGroupRefs` returns on an undeclared object. No door can produce a false warning from an absent object. The draft save returns before any collection read (D1), so it runs no rule, as the card and the dev state.
3. **Nothing is refused; `valid` cannot flip** — right. `validateFormLayout` emits `severity: 'warning'` only, and `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` splits on the finding's severity (`errors` = `error`, `advisories` = the rest), so the gate's `error` is never built from these findings; a rule throw is itself caught into a warning (`authoring-rule-threw`). On the read, `withFormLayoutWarnings` keeps `valid` from the prior verdict (or `true`), and `withPublishVerdict` folds only the gate's refusal `issues`. Pinned: an active save answers two warning advisories and `success: true`, the publish of a draft naming an unknown field answers `success: true`, and the read after both answers `valid: true`.
4. **One finding, once, on the read** — right. The read's only runtime judgement is `draftPublishVerdict` → `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules`, whose advisories are discarded (`verdict.error.issues` only). So the rule's output reaches `_diagnostics` through `withFormLayoutWarnings` alone, and it runs once per read. The draft read now runs the rule a second time inside the gate for no output; that is a pure walk over objects the gate already gathers for the other `view` rules, no new read. Pinned on the active read after the active save (each message once) and on the form item read (one warning at `config.sections.0.fields.1`).
5. **`formLayoutSubject` retired, paths byte-identical** — right. The old adapter handed `{ name, object, form: config }` and rewrote the leading `form` to `config`; the rule now yields the site at `${viewPath}.config` itself, and `itemRelativeIssuePath('view', name, 'views[0].config.sections[0].fields[1]')` strips `views[0]`, dots the indices and the leading dot, giving `config.sections.0.fields.1` — the exact #29196 pin, which is unchanged in the file and green on the head. The binding order is the same as the adapter's (`config.data.object` → the item's `object`, via `viewObjectName(site.view) ?? containerObject`). The `formViews.edit.sections.0.fields.0` pin is untouched. One observable difference: `spelledObjectNames` now walks the whole served item instead of the trimmed subject, which can only add `getObject` map lookups for names the item spells elsewhere; a name the lookup does not answer is not judged, so no new finding and no false one.
6. **The `config` rung cannot throw or misfire** — right. It is keyed on `view.viewKind === 'form' && isRec(view.config)`; a list item (`viewKind: 'list'`, pinned), a form item whose `config` is missing, an array or a scalar, and any non-item container shape do not get the site. Inside the site every read is guarded as before: `sections`/`groups` must be arrays, a section must be a record, `fields` must be an array, an entry is a string or `{ field }`. A form item carries no root `sections`, `form` or `formViews`, so the shared ladder yields nothing for it and the `config` site is the only one: no double finding. `recordsOf(obj.fieldGroups)` tolerates an array, a record or nothing. Rule ids, messages, hints, `where` spelling and severity are unchanged; the rung is in this rule only, `view-walk.ts` is untouched, so no other walker's verdict moves.
7. **Forced test edits** — justified. The #29196 stub's `listItems('object')` listing `authoredTask` was a universe no real registry answers (`listItems` → `getAllObjects` → `resolveObject`, the same merged object `getObject` serves); with it the gate would have charged the extension field `region__c` as unknown on save. Listing `servedTask` is the measured shape; the fixture's one `fieldGroups` entry is what the group control needs. The five view rule-list pins (three in `runtime-gate.test.ts`, one each in `authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts` and `runtime-gate.page-visibility-predicate-writes.test.ts`) enumerate `runtimeAuthoringRulesFor('view')` in registry order and gain exactly the one entry at the one slot the registry gives it; all green on the head.
8. **Cost** — right. `withFormLayoutWarnings` is called at one site only, the item read (`getMetaItem`, `protocol.ts` 5473); no list read runs it. The gate's five collection reads already ran for every active `view` write (the type already carried runtime rules); the new rule walks those objects and reads nothing else. The view read loses the adapter.
9. **CLI surface** — the rung is also seen by `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` (`commands: ALL`), so a stack carrying a Studio-shaped form item now warns there too; additive warnings on an advisory rule, named in the changeset.

Design judgment on the two cited rules files (folded here; the declaration face carries no ④): the change holds against the code it cites and the card's acceptance — both findings answered as warnings on save and publish through the real door, `form-section-group-unknown` on the read, red-first pins and a control on each. I tried to break it on the paths above (absent object, cross-package object, malformed `config`, list item, draft save, batch publish, the read's double) and found no false warning, no refusal and no second report.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/lint: patch`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` — right. Nothing published changes shape: the 2xx `advisories[]` and `_diagnostics.warnings[]` gain entries of their existing element shape, `valid` and every status are unchanged, no key, schema or export is added or removed (`FORM_SECTION_GROUP_UNKNOWN` was already exported from the lint root). `Clause-②: no` is right for the same reason, and `Metadata-protocol: none` is right (no door, verb or address moves). The changeset text matches the diff, D1 included.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, draft save carries no advisory (D1, open question 2 of 6579051645): answered — contract unchanged by the seat's amendment; the tree agrees (`judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules` returns before any collection read on `state !== 'active'`), and the draft read and the publish both carry the finding. Pinned.
- Open question 1 (form ViewItem's `config` not walked): closed by amendment 6579089637 (option A); the rung is on this PR, within the amended surface (`validate-form-layout.ts`, view walk only), and the PR is `Fixes #29309`.
- Delta report's `open_questions: []`: nothing left open.
- Claim surface: `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` (held by PR #29226), `ui/**`, `packages/spec/**` untouched; the only lint rule-logic change is the one the amendment admits.
- Residual, not a fix: the boot measurement's control named real fields only; the declared-group control is pinned on the stub (`fieldGroups` on the served object) and holds by reading (`resolveObject` folds onto a spread of the base definition, `fieldGroups` kept).
- Should-fix, non-blocking: `packages/lint/src/validate-form-layout.test.ts` splices the new `#29309` describe into the middle of the `[#22161] Slice 21` comment block (its last line, "members is the id's `os explain` entry.", is now orphaned above the `[#22161]` describe). Move the new block below that describe, or above the comment.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no non-fleet login to name.

Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmQxwoGb5fSnrFkpxmt`

**VERDICT: PASS**
